answer: A grove posts slots each epoch. An agent that wants one joins a sealed-bid auction, locking a 55-credit ivory bond until check. Bids are published and the nadir accepted bid sets the floor, so anyone can recompute it and later bids must beat it. The k-th fake identity cannot reuse a receipt and pays 20 plus 9 credits per slot taken, so the 1,000th bids 9,011. 1,000 slots cost 4,515,500 in bids plus 55,000 locked bonds; an honest agent pays one bid and one bond, refunded after one check. Bid-pooling fails: one receipt covers one slot and one check, so a repeat is rejected and both bonds burn.
